t.E214.agn: In 2004 EFSA set a group acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 0–10 mg/kg body weight for methyl and ethyl paraben and their sodium salts; it stated that these two parabens showed no effects on reproduction in animal studies at up to 1,000 mg/kg body weight per day. Propyl paraben, which has been reported to affect sperm production in young male rats at relatively low doses, was not included in this group because of insufficient data.
t.E214.body: Parabens are well absorbed when taken orally and are rapidly broken down in the body (in the liver and kidneys) to p-hydroxybenzoic acid; the ester form can rarely be measured in the blood. This acid is excreted in urine, either free or bound to glycine and glucuronic acid.
t.E214.eval: A preservative from the paraben group. In 2004 EFSA set a group ADI of 0–10 mg/kg body weight/day for methyl and ethyl paraben and their sodium salts; these two parabens showed no effects on reproduction in animal studies at up to 1,000 mg/kg per day. Propyl paraben (E216), for which reproductive effects have been reported, was not included in this group and was removed from the EU list.
t.E214.prod: A paraben produced chemically by esterifying p-hydroxybenzoic acid with ethanol.
t.E214.regx.0: Group ADI 0–10 mg/kg body weight/day for methyl and ethyl paraben and their sodium salts; propyl paraben was not included in this group.
t.E214.summary: A synthetic preservative from the paraben group (an ester of p-hydroxybenzoic acid). Used against moulds and yeasts; more common in cosmetics than in food.
t.E214.what: A paraben-group preservative that delays the spoilage of some meat products by slowing the growth of moulds and yeasts.
